How Git Sync Works Between Devices

Think of GitHub as a shared mailbox. Each device drops off and picks up the latest version.
Dell
C:\Users\russe\Obsidian\
knowledge-vault\
⟶
git push
⟵
git pull
GitHub
russalo/knowledge-vault
(private repo)
⟶
git push
⟵
git pull
iPhone
~/Documents/
knowledge-vault/
Key concept: Each device has its own complete copy of all the files. GitHub is the middleman — the central copy that everyone syncs to. No device talks directly to another device. They all go through GitHub.

Scenario 1: You edit a note on the Dell, then read it on your phone

1
Dell — Obsidian
You open Obsidian, edit PKP/TASKS.md — add a new task.
What Dell's files look like now:
PKP/TASKS.md — modified (new task added)
PKP/DECISIONS.md — unchanged
TIQ/VISION.md — unchanged
2
Dell — Obsidian Git plugin (automatic)
After 5 minutes, the plugin auto-commits and pushes your change to GitHub.
git add . → git commit → git push
3
GitHub
GitHub now has the updated PKP/TASKS.md. It stores the new version and the history of what changed.
GitHub's copy now matches the Dell's copy:
PKP/TASKS.md — v2 (has your new task)
PKP/DECISIONS.md — v1
TIQ/VISION.md — v1
4
iPhone — you tap "Vault Pull" shortcut
Your phone asks GitHub: "What's new?" GitHub sends down the updated PKP/TASKS.md.
lg2 pull
5
iPhone — Obsidian
Open Obsidian. Your new task is right there. Done.
What happened: Dell → GitHub → iPhone. The file traveled through GitHub. At no point did the Dell and iPhone talk directly. That's the whole model.

Scenario 2: You capture a thought on your phone, then see it on the Dell

1
iPhone — Quick Capture shortcut
You're on a job site. Tap "Quick Capture", type: "Check if Mini needs UPS for power outages"
2
iPhone — Shortcut appends + syncs
The shortcut appends a timestamped line to PKP/INBOX.md, commits, and pushes to GitHub. All in one tap.
append to INBOX.md → lg2 add → lg2 commit → lg2 push
PKP/INBOX.md on GitHub now contains:
# [PKP] Inbox
Items awaiting triage.
---
- [2026-03-28 14:32] Check if Mini needs UPS for power outages
3
Dell — Obsidian opens
You open Obsidian on the Dell later. The Obsidian Git plugin auto-pulls on startup. Your captured thought is sitting in INBOX.md.
git pull (automatic on startup)
This is the bottleneck killer. Thought captured in 5 seconds on a job site. Available on the Dell, BossDev, or Mini when you sit down to triage. No Chat threads, no lost context.

Scenario 3: What happens when two devices edit the same file?

1
Dell
You add "Buy monitor cable" to PKP/TASKS.md on the Dell. Obsidian Git pushes it.
2
iPhone — forgot to pull first!
Without pulling, you add "Call electrician" to PKP/TASKS.md on your phone. You tap "Vault Sync".
Now there's a conflict:
Dell version: "...Buy monitor cable"
Phone version: "...Call electrician"
GitHub doesn't know which version is right!
3
iPhone — push fails
Git says: "Rejected — the remote has changes you don't have." Your push doesn't go through. Nothing is lost.
4
Fix it on the Dell
Pull on the Dell. Git marks the conflict in the file. You open it, keep both lines, remove the conflict markers, commit, push. Done.
Resolved — both changes kept:
- Buy monitor cable
- Call electrician
How to avoid this: Always pull before editing. That one habit eliminates 99% of conflicts. The .gitignore file already excludes workspace files (the biggest conflict source). Real content conflicts only happen if you edit the same file on two devices without syncing in between.

Scenario 4: Claude Code on BossDev reads and writes to the vault

1
BossDev — SSH session
You SSH into BossDev. Pull the latest vault.
cd ~/knowledge-vault && git pull
2
BossDev — Claude Code
Run Claude Code in the vault directory. Ask it to triage PKP/INBOX.md, draft routing proposals, or update docs.
cd ~/knowledge-vault && claude
3
BossDev — push changes
Claude Code made changes. Commit and push.
git add . && git commit -m "triage: routed 5 inbox items" && git push
4
Dell — next time Obsidian opens
Auto-pull grabs the changes Claude Code made. You review them in Obsidian.
This is the automation path. Eventually, a cron job on BossDev or Mini could do this automatically — pull vault, run triage, push results. You review on the Dell or phone.

The Rules

1. Always pull before editing on any device.
2. Always push when done — don't leave unpushed changes overnight.
3. One device at a time on the same file.
4. If something goes wrong, fix it on the Dell — desktop tools are best for conflicts.
5. Git never deletes without you asking. Your work is safe.
